entries.short_description: The product violates the Enterprise JavaBeans (EJB) specification by using the class loader.

entries.name: J2EE Bad Practices: Non-serializable Object Stored in Session
entries.short_description: The product stores a non-serializable object as an HttpSession attribute, which can hurt reliability.

entries.name: Path Equivalence: Windows 8.3 Filename
entries.short_description: The product contains a protection mechanism that restricts access to a long filename on a Windows operating system, but it does not properly restrict access to the equivalent short "8.3" filename.

entries.name: clone() Method Without super.clone()
entries.short_description: The product contains a clone() method that does not call super.clone() to obtain the new object.

entries.name: Object Model Violation: Just One of Equals and Hashcode Defined
entries.short_description: The product does not maintain equal hashcodes for equal objects.

entries.name: Array Declared Public, Final, and Static
entries.short_description: The product declares an array public, final, and static, which is not sufficient to prevent the array's contents from being modified.

entries.name: finalize() Method Declared Public
entries.short_description: The product violates secure coding principles for mobile code by declaring a finalize() method public.

entries.name: Return Inside Finally Block
entries.short_description: The code has a return statement inside a finally block, which will cause any thrown exception in the try block to be discarded.

entries.name: Empty Synchronized Block
entries.short_description: The product contains an empty synchronized block.

entries.name: Explicit Call to Finalize()
entries.short_description: The product makes an explicit call to the finalize() method from outside the finalizer.

entries.name: Assignment of a Fixed Address to a Pointer
entries.short_description: The product sets a pointer to a specific address other than NULL or 0.

entries.name: Attempt to Access Child of a Non-structure Pointer
entries.short_description: Casting a non-structure type to a structure type and accessing a field can lead to memory access errors or data corruption.

entries.name: Call to Non-ubiquitous API
entries.short_description: The product uses an API function that does not exist on all versions of the target platform. This could cause portability problems or inconsistencies that allow denial of service or other consequences.

entries.name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
entries.short_description: The product attempts to access a file based on the filename, but it does not properly prevent that filename from identifying a link or shortcut that resolves to an unintended resource.

entries.name: Free of Memory not on the Heap
entries.short_description: The product calls free() on a pointer to memory that was not allocated using associated heap allocation functions such as malloc(), calloc(), or realloc().

entries.name: Sensitive Data Storage in Improperly Locked Memory
entries.short_description: The product stores sensitive data in memory that is not locked, or that has been incorrectly locked, which might cause the memory to be written to swap files on disk by the virtual memory manager. This can make the data more accessible to external actors.

entries.name: Authentication Bypass: OpenSSL CTX Object Modified after SSL Objects are Created
entries.short_description: The product modifies the SSL context after connection creation has begun.

entries.name: J2EE Framework: Saving Unserializable Objects to Disk
entries.short_description: When the J2EE container attempts to write unserializable objects to disk there is no guarantee that the process will complete successfully.

entries.name: Comparison of Object References Instead of Object Contents
entries.short_description: The product compares object references instead of the contents of the objects themselves, preventing it from detecting equivalent objects.

entries.name: DEPRECATED: Incorrect Semantic Object Comparison
entries.short_description: This weakness has been deprecated. It was poorly described and difficult to distinguish from other entries. It was also inappropriate to assign a separate ID solely because of domain-specific considerations.

entries.name: Use of Wrong Operator in String Comparison
entries.short_description: The product uses the wrong operator when comparing a string, such as using "==" when the .equals() method should be used instead.

entries.name: Use of HTTP Request With Sensitive Query String
entries.short_description: The web application uses an HTTP method to process a request, but the request includes sensitive information in the query string.

entries.name: Missing Validation of OpenSSL Certificate
entries.short_description: The product uses OpenSSL and trusts or uses a certificate without using the SSL_get_verify_result() function to ensure that the certificate satisfies all necessary security requirements.

entries.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Insufficient Session-ID Length
entries.short_description: The J2EE application is configured to use an insufficient session ID length.

entries.name: Uncaught Exception in Servlet
entries.short_description: The Servlet does not catch all exceptions, which may reveal sensitive debugging information.

entries.name: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')
entries.short_description: The web application accepts a user-controlled input that specifies a link to an external site, and uses that link in a redirect.

entries.name: Use of Client-Side Authentication
entries.short_description: A client/server product performs authentication within client code but not in server code, allowing server-side authentication to be bypassed via a modified client that omits the authentication check.

entries.name: Multiple Binds to the Same Port
entries.short_description: When multiple sockets are allowed to bind to the same port, other services on that port may be stolen or spoofed.

entries.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition
entries.short_description: The product does not properly check inputs that are used for loop conditions, potentially leading to a denial of service or other consequences because of excessive looping.

entries.name: Public Static Final Field References Mutable Object
entries.short_description: A public or protected static final field references a mutable object, which allows the object to be changed by malicious code, or accidentally from another package.

entries.name: Struts: Non-private Field in ActionForm Class
entries.short_description: An ActionForm class contains a field that has not been declared private, which can be accessed without using a setter or getter.

entries.name: Double-Checked Locking
entries.short_description: The product uses double-checked locking to access a resource without the overhead of explicit synchronization, but the locking is insufficient.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
entries.short_description: The product processes an XML document that can contain XML entities with URIs that resolve to documents outside of the intended sphere of control, causing the product to embed incorrect documents into its output.

entries.name: Improper Authorization of Index Containing Sensitive Information
entries.short_description: The product creates a search index of private or sensitive documents, but it does not properly limit index access to actors who are authorized to see the original information.

entries.name: Insufficient Session Expiration
entries.short_description: According to WASC, "Insufficient Session Expiration is when a web site permits an attacker to reuse old session credentials or session IDs for authorization."

entries.name: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute
entries.short_description: The Secure attribute for sensitive cookies in HTTPS sessions is not set.

entries.name: Inclusion of Sensitive Information in Source Code Comments
entries.short_description: While adding general comments is very useful, some programmers tend to leave important data, such as: filenames related to the web application, old links or links which were not meant to be browsed by users, old code fragments, etc.

entries.name: Incomplete Identification of Uploaded File Variables (PHP)
entries.short_description: The PHP application uses an old method for processing uploaded files by referencing the four global variables that are set for each file (e.g. $varname, $varname_size, $varname_name, $varname_type). These variables could be overwritten by attackers, causing the application to process unauthorized files.

entries.name: Reachable Assertion
entries.short_description: The product contains an assert() or similar statement that can be triggered by an attacker, which leads to an application exit or other behavior that is more severe than necessary.

entries.name: Exposed Unsafe ActiveX Method
entries.short_description: An ActiveX control is intended for use in a web browser, but it exposes dangerous methods that perform actions that are outside of the browser's security model (e.g. the zone or domain).

entries.name: Dangling Database Cursor ('Cursor Injection')
entries.short_description: If a database cursor is not closed properly, then it could become accessible to other users while retaining the same privileges that were originally assigned, leaving the cursor "dangling."

entries.name: UNIX Hard Link
entries.short_description: The product, when opening a file or directory, does not sufficiently account for when the name is associated with a hard link to a target that is outside of the intended control sphere. This could allow an attacker to cause the product to operate on unauthorized files.

entries.name: Unverified Password Change
entries.short_description: When setting a new password for a user, the product does not require knowledge of the original password, or using another form of authentication.

entries.name: Variable Extraction Error
entries.short_description: The product uses external input to determine the names of variables into which information is extracted, without verifying that the names of the specified variables are valid. This could cause the program to overwrite unintended variables.

entries.name: Improper Validation of Function Hook Arguments
entries.short_description: The product adds hooks to user-accessible API functions, but it does not properly validate the arguments. This could lead to resultant vulnerabilities.

entries.name: Unsafe ActiveX Control Marked Safe For Scripting
entries.short_description: An ActiveX control is intended for restricted use, but it has been marked as safe-for-scripting.

entries.name: Executable Regular Expression Error
entries.short_description: The product uses a regular expression that either (1) contains an executable component with user-controlled inputs, or (2) allows a user to enable execution by inserting pattern modifiers.

entries.name: Permissive Regular Expression
entries.short_description: The product uses a regular expression that does not sufficiently restrict the set of allowed values.

entries.name: Null Byte Interaction Error (Poison Null Byte)
entries.short_description: The product does not properly handle null bytes or NUL characters when passing data between different representations or components.

entries.name: Dynamic Variable Evaluation
entries.short_description: In a language where the user can influence the name of a variable at runtime, if the variable names are not controlled, an attacker can read or write to arbitrary variables, or access arbitrary functions.

entries.name: Function Call with Incorrectly Specified Arguments
entries.short_description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine with arguments that are not correctly specified, leading to always-incorrect behavior and resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
entries.short_description: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

entries.name: Windows Shortcut Following (.LNK)
entries.short_description: The product, when opening a file or directory, does not sufficiently handle when the file is a Windows shortcut (.LNK) whose target is outside of the intended control sphere. This could allow an attacker to cause the product to operate on unauthorized files.

entries.name: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
entries.short_description: The product contains a mechanism for users to recover or change their passwords without knowing the original password, but the mechanism is weak.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of Names for Files and Other Resources
entries.short_description: The product constructs the name of a file or other resource using input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the resulting name.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')
entries.short_description: The product uses external input to dynamically construct an XPath expression used to retrieve data from an XML database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes that input. This allows an attacker to control the structure of the query.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of HTTP Headers for Scripting Syntax
entries.short_description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes web scripting syntax in HTTP headers that can be used by web browser components that can process raw headers, such as Flash.

entries.name: Overly Restrictive Account Lockout Mechanism
entries.short_description: The product contains an account lockout protection mechanism, but the mechanism is too restrictive and can be triggered too easily, which allows attackers to deny service to legitimate users by causing their accounts to be locked out.

entries.name: Reliance on File Name or Extension of Externally-Supplied File
entries.short_description: The product allows a file to be uploaded, but it relies on the file name or extension of the file to determine the appropriate behaviors. This could be used by attackers to cause the file to be misclassified and processed in a dangerous fashion.

entries.name: Use of Non-Canonical URL Paths for Authorization Decisions
entries.short_description: The product defines policy namespaces and makes authorization decisions based on the assumption that a URL is canonical. This can allow a non-canonical URL to bypass the authorization.

entries.name: Incorrect Use of Privileged APIs
entries.short_description: The product does not conform to the API requirements for a function call that requires extra privileges. This could allow attackers to gain privileges by causing the function to be called incorrectly.

entries.name: Reliance on Obfuscation or Encryption of Security-Relevant Inputs without Integrity Checking
entries.short_description: The product uses obfuscation or encryption of inputs that should not be mutable by an external actor, but the product does not use integrity checks to detect if those inputs have been modified.

entries.name: Windows Hard Link
entries.short_description: The product, when opening a file or directory, does not sufficiently handle when the name is associated with a hard link to a target that is outside of the intended control sphere. This could allow an attacker to cause the product to operate on unauthorized files.

entries.name: Trusting HTTP Permission Methods on the Server Side
entries.short_description: The server contains a protection mechanism that assumes that any URI that is accessed using HTTP GET will not cause a state change to the associated resource. This might allow attackers to bypass intended access restrictions and conduct resource modification and deletion attacks, since some applications allow GET to modify state.

entries.name: Exposure of WSDL File Containing Sensitive Information
entries.short_description: The Web services architecture may require exposing a Web Service Definition Language (WSDL) file that contains information on the publicly accessible services and how callers of these services should interact with them (e.g. what parameters they expect and what types they return).

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Data within XQuery Expressions ('XQuery Injection')
entries.short_description: The product uses external input to dynamically construct an XQuery expression used to retrieve data from an XML database, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes that input. This allows an attacker to control the structure of the query.

entries.name: Reliance on a Single Factor in a Security Decision
entries.short_description: A protection mechanism relies exclusively, or to a large extent, on the evaluation of a single condition or the integrity of a single object or entity in order to make a decision about granting access to restricted resources or functionality.

entries.name: Improper Handling of File Names that Identify Virtual Resources
entries.short_description: The product does not handle or incorrectly handles a file name that identifies a "virtual" resource that is not directly specified within the directory that is associated with the file name, causing the product to perform file-based operations on a resource that is not a file.

entries.name: Use of a Non-reentrant Function in a Concurrent Context
entries.short_description: The product calls a non-reentrant function in a concurrent context in which a competing code sequence (e.g. thread or signal handler) may have an opportunity to call the same function or otherwise influence its state.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Windows Device Names
entries.short_description: The product constructs pathnames from user input, but it does not handle or incorrectly handles a pathname containing a Windows device name such as AUX or CON. This typically leads to denial of service or an information exposure when the application attempts to process the pathname as a regular file.

entries.name: Use of Potentially Dangerous Function
entries.short_description: The product invokes a potentially dangerous function that could introduce a vulnerability if it is used incorrectly, but the function can also be used safely.

entries.name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
entries.short_description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.

entries.name: Function Call With Incorrect Order of Arguments
entries.short_description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies the arguments in an incorrect order, leading to resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Function Call With Incorrect Number of Arguments
entries.short_description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies too many arguments, or too few arguments, which may lead to undefined behavior and resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Function Call With Incorrect Argument Type
entries.short_description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies an argument that is the wrong data type, which may lead to resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Function Call With Incorrectly Specified Argument Value
entries.short_description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies an argument that contains the wrong value, which may lead to resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Function Call With Incorrect Variable or Reference as Argument
entries.short_description: The product calls a function, procedure, or routine, but the caller specifies the wrong variable or reference as one of the arguments, which may lead to undefined behavior and resultant weaknesses.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Windows ::DATA Alternate Data Stream
entries.short_description: The product does not properly prevent access to, or detect usage of, alternate data streams (ADS).

entries.name: Use of Multiple Resources with Duplicate Identifier
entries.short_description: The product uses multiple resources that can have the same identifier, in a context in which unique identifiers are required.

entries.name: Use of Low-Level Functionality
entries.short_description: The product uses low-level functionality that is explicitly prohibited by the framework or specification under which the product is supposed to operate.

entries.name: Execution After Redirect (EAR)
entries.short_description: The web application sends a redirect to another location, but instead of exiting, it executes additional code.

entries.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Missing Custom Error Page
entries.short_description: The default error page of a web application should not display sensitive information about the product.

entries.name: Incorrect Ownership Assignment
entries.short_description: The product assigns an owner to a resource, but the owner is outside of the intended control sphere.

entries.name: DEPRECATED: Apple '.DS_Store'
entries.short_description: This entry has been deprecated as it represents a specific observed example of a UNIX Hard Link weakness type rather than its own individual weakness type. Please refer to CWE-62.

entries.name: Improper Handling of Apple HFS+ Alternate Data Stream Path
entries.short_description: The product does not properly handle special paths that may identify the data or resource fork of a file on the HFS+ file system.

entries.name: External Control of File Name or Path
entries.short_description: The product allows user input to control or influence paths or file names that are used in filesystem operations.

entries.name: Compiler Optimization Removal or Modification of Security-critical Code
entries.short_description: The developer builds a security-critical protection mechanism into the software, but the compiler optimizes the program such that the mechanism is removed or modified.

entries.name: Exposed Dangerous Method or Function
entries.short_description: The product provides an Applications Programming Interface (API) or similar interface for interaction with external actors, but the interface includes a dangerous method or function that is not properly restricted.

entries.name: Missing Custom Error Page
entries.short_description: The product does not return custom error pages to the user, possibly exposing sensitive information.

entries.name: Selection of Less-Secure Algorithm During Negotiation ('Algorithm Downgrade')
entries.short_description: A protocol or its implementation supports interaction between multiple actors and allows those actors to negotiate which algorithm should be used as a protection mechanism such as encryption or authentication, but it does not select the strongest algorithm that is available to both parties.

entries.name: Use of a One-Way Hash without a Salt
entries.short_description: The product uses a one-way cryptographic hash against an input that should not be reversible, such as a password, but the product does not also use a salt as part of the input.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Equivalent Special Elements
entries.short_description: The product correctly neutralizes certain special elements, but it improperly neutralizes equivalent special elements.

entries.name: Use of a One-Way Hash with a Predictable Salt
entries.short_description: The product uses a one-way cryptographic hash against an input that should not be reversible, such as a password, but the product uses a predictable salt as part of the input.

entries.name: Free of Pointer not at Start of Buffer
entries.short_description: The product calls free() on a pointer to a memory resource that was allocated on the heap, but the pointer is not at the start of the buffer.

entries.name: Mismatched Memory Management Routines
entries.short_description: The product attempts to return a memory resource to the system, but it calls a release function that is not compatible with the function that was originally used to allocate that resource.

entries.name: Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference
entries.short_description: The product attempts to return a memory resource to the system, but it calls the wrong release function or calls the appropriate release function incorrectly.

entries.name: Multiple Locks of a Critical Resource
entries.short_description: The product locks a critical resource more times than intended, leading to an unexpected state in the system.

entries.name: Multiple Unlocks of a Critical Resource
entries.short_description: The product unlocks a critical resource more times than intended, leading to an unexpected state in the system.

entries.name: Critical Data Element Declared Public
entries.short_description: The product declares a critical variable, field, or member to be public when intended security policy requires it to be private.

entries.name: Access to Critical Private Variable via Public Method
entries.short_description: The product defines a public method that reads or modifies a private variable.

entries.name: Incorrect Short Circuit Evaluation
entries.short_description: The product contains a conditional statement with multiple logical expressions in which one of the non-leading expressions may produce side effects. This may lead to an unexpected state in the program after the execution of the conditional, because short-circuiting logic may prevent the side effects from occurring.

entries.name: DEPRECATED: Uncontrolled File Descriptor Consumption
entries.short_description: This entry has been deprecated because it was a duplicate of CWE-774. All content has been transferred to CWE-774.

entries.name: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
entries.short_description: The product allocates a reusable resource or group of resources on behalf of an actor without imposing any intended restrictions on the size or number of resources that can be allocated.

entries.name: Missing Reference to Active Allocated Resource
entries.short_description: The product does not properly maintain a reference to a resource that has been allocated, which prevents the resource from being reclaimed.

entries.name: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
entries.short_description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

entries.name: Missing Reference to Active File Descriptor or Handle
entries.short_description: The product does not properly maintain references to a file descriptor or handle, which prevents that file descriptor/handle from being reclaimed.

entries.name: Allocation of File Descriptors or Handles Without Limits or Throttling
entries.short_description: The product allocates file descriptors or handles on behalf of an actor without imposing any restrictions on how many descriptors can be allocated, in violation of the intended security policy for that actor.

entries.name: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
entries.short_description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')
entries.short_description: The product uses XML documents and allows their structure to be defined with a Document Type Definition (DTD), but it does not properly control the number of recursive definitions of entities.

entries.name: Regular Expression without Anchors
entries.short_description: The product uses a regular expression to perform neutralization, but the regular expression is not anchored and may allow malicious or malformed data to slip through.

entries.name: Insufficient Logging
entries.short_description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

entries.name: Logging of Excessive Data
entries.short_description: The product logs too much information, making log files hard to process and possibly hindering recovery efforts or forensic analysis after an attack.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
entries.short_description: The product constructs all or part of an OS command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended OS command when it is sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Use of RSA Algorithm without OAEP
entries.short_description: The product uses the RSA algorithm but does not incorporate Optimal Asymmetric Encryption Padding (OAEP), which might weaken the encryption.

entries.name: Improper Address Validation in IOCTL with METHOD_NEITHER I/O Control Code
entries.short_description: The product defines an IOCTL that uses METHOD_NEITHER for I/O, but it does not validate or incorrectly validates the addresses that are provided.

entries.name: Exposed IOCTL with Insufficient Access Control
entries.short_description: The product implements an IOCTL with functionality that should be restricted, but it does not properly enforce access control for the IOCTL.

entries.name: Operator Precedence Logic Error
entries.short_description: The product uses an expression in which operator precedence causes incorrect logic to be used.

entries.name: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking in a Security Decision
entries.short_description: The product uses a protection mechanism that relies on the existence or values of a cookie, but it does not properly ensure that the cookie is valid for the associated user.

entries.name: Use of Path Manipulation Function without Maximum-sized Buffer
entries.short_description: The product invokes a function for normalizing paths or file names, but it provides an output buffer that is smaller than the maximum possible size, such as PATH_MAX.

entries.name: Access of Memory Location Before Start of Buffer
entries.short_description: The product reads or writes to a buffer using an index or pointer that references a memory location prior to the beginning of the buffer.

entries.name: Out-of-bounds Write
entries.short_description: The product writes data past the end, or before the beginning, of the intended buffer.

entries.name: Access of Memory Location After End of Buffer
entries.short_description: The product reads or writes to a buffer using an index or pointer that references a memory location after the end of the buffer.

entries.name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
entries.short_description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
entries.short_description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.

entries.name: Incomplete Filtering of Special Elements
entries.short_description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but does not completely filter special elements before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Incomplete Filtering of One or More Instances of Special Elements
entries.short_description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but does not completely filter one or more instances of special elements before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Only Filtering One Instance of a Special Element
entries.short_description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only filters a single instance of a special element before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Incomplete Filtering of Multiple Instances of Special Elements
entries.short_description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but does not filter all instances of a special element before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Only Filtering Special Elements at a Specified Location
entries.short_description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements at a specified location, thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Only Filtering Special Elements Relative to a Marker
entries.short_description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements positioned relative to a marker (e.g. "at the beginning/end of a string; the second argument"), thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Only Filtering Special Elements at an Absolute Position
entries.short_description: The product receives data from an upstream component, but only accounts for special elements at an absolute position (e.g. "byte number 10"), thereby missing remaining special elements that may exist before sending it to a downstream component.

entries.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
entries.short_description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

entries.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Entity Bean Declared Remote
entries.short_description: When an application exposes a remote interface for an entity bean, it might also expose methods that get or set the bean's data. These methods could be leveraged to read sensitive information, or to change data in ways that violate the application's expectations, potentially leading to other vulnerabilities.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS)
entries.short_description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special characters such as "<", ">", and "&" that could be interpreted as web-scripting elements when they are sent to a downstream component that processes web pages.

entries.name: Guessable CAPTCHA
entries.short_description: The product uses a CAPTCHA challenge, but the challenge can be guessed or automatically recognized by a non-human actor.

entries.name: Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value
entries.short_description: The product uses a sequential operation to read or write a buffer, but it uses an incorrect length value that causes it to access memory that is outside of the bounds of the buffer.

entries.name: Buffer Access Using Size of Source Buffer
entries.short_description: The product uses the size of a source buffer when reading from or writing to a destination buffer, which may cause it to access memory that is outside of the bounds of the buffer.

entries.name: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
entries.short_description: The product uses a protection mechanism that relies on the existence or values of an input, but the input can be modified by an untrusted actor in a way that bypasses the protection mechanism.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in an Error Message Web Page
entries.short_description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special characters that could be interpreted as web-scripting elements when they are sent to an error page.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes of IMG Tags in a Web Page
entries.short_description: The web application does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes scripting elements within attributes of HTML IMG tags, such as the src attribute.

entries.name: Missing Synchronization
entries.short_description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

entries.name: Incorrect Synchronization
entries.short_description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner, but it does not correctly synchronize access to the resource.

entries.name: Untrusted Pointer Dereference
entries.short_description: The product obtains a value from an untrusted source, converts this value to a pointer, and dereferences the resulting pointer.

entries.name: Use of Out-of-range Pointer Offset
entries.short_description: The product performs pointer arithmetic on a valid pointer, but it uses an offset that can point outside of the intended range of valid memory locations for the resulting pointer.

entries.name: Access of Uninitialized Pointer
entries.short_description: The product accesses or uses a pointer that has not been initialized.

entries.name: Expired Pointer Dereference
entries.short_description: The product dereferences a pointer that contains a location for memory that was previously valid, but is no longer valid.

entries.name: Premature Release of Resource During Expected Lifetime
entries.short_description: The product releases a resource that is still intended to be used by itself or another actor.

entries.name: Improper Control of Document Type Definition
entries.short_description: The product does not restrict a reference to a Document Type Definition (DTD) to the intended control sphere. This might allow attackers to reference arbitrary DTDs, possibly causing the product to expose files, consume excessive system resources, or execute arbitrary http requests on behalf of the attacker.

entries.name: Signal Handler with Functionality that is not Asynchronous-Safe
entries.short_description: The product defines a signal handler that contains code sequences that are not asynchronous-safe, i.e., the functionality is not reentrant, or it can be interrupted.

entries.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
entries.short_description: The product imports, requires, or includes executable functionality (such as a library) from a source that is outside of the intended control sphere.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Script in Attributes in a Web Page
entries.short_description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes "javascript:" or other URIs from dangerous attributes within tags, such as onmouseover, onload, onerror, or style.

entries.name: Inclusion of Web Functionality from an Untrusted Source
entries.short_description: The product includes web functionality (such as a web widget) from another domain, which causes it to operate within the domain of the product, potentially granting total access and control of the product to the untrusted source.

entries.name: Signal Handler Function Associated with Multiple Signals
entries.short_description: The product defines a function that is used as a handler for more than one signal.

entries.name: Unlock of a Resource that is not Locked
entries.short_description: The product attempts to unlock a resource that is not locked.

entries.name: Deadlock
entries.short_description: The product contains multiple threads or executable segments that are waiting for each other to release a necessary lock, resulting in deadlock.

entries.name: Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop')
entries.short_description: The product contains an iteration or loop with an exit condition that cannot be reached, i.e., an infinite loop.

entries.name: Use of Password Hash Instead of Password for Authentication
entries.short_description: The product records password hashes in a data store, receives a hash of a password from a client, and compares the supplied hash to the hash obtained from the data store.

entries.name: Improper Enforcement of a Single, Unique Action
entries.short_description: The product requires that an actor should only be able to perform an action once, or to have only one unique action, but the product does not enforce or improperly enforces this restriction.

entries.name: Inappropriate Encoding for Output Context
entries.short_description: The product uses or specifies an encoding when generating output to a downstream component, but the specified encoding is not the same as the encoding that is expected by the downstream component.

entries.name: Numeric Range Comparison Without Minimum Check
entries.short_description: The product checks a value to ensure that it is less than or equal to a maximum, but it does not also verify that the value is greater than or equal to the minimum.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Encoded URI Schemes in a Web Page
entries.short_description: The web application improperly neutralizes user-controlled input for executable script disguised with URI encodings.

entries.name: Placement of User into Incorrect Group
entries.short_description: The product or the administrator places a user into an incorrect group.

entries.name: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
entries.short_description: The product allocates or initializes a resource such as a pointer, object, or variable using one type, but it later accesses that resource using a type that is incompatible with the original type.

entries.name: Doubled Character XSS Manipulations
entries.short_description: The web application does not filter user-controlled input for executable script disguised using doubling of the involved characters.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Invalid Characters in Identifiers in Web Pages
entries.short_description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes invalid characters or byte sequences in the middle of tag names, URI schemes, and other identifiers.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Alternate XSS Syntax
entries.short_description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controlled input for alternate script syntax.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
entries.short_description: The product constructs a string for a command to be executed by a separate component in another control sphere, but it does not properly delimit the intended arguments, options, or switches within that command string.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
entries.short_description: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is sent to a downstream component. Without sufficient removal or quoting of SQL syntax in user-controllable inputs, the generated SQL query can cause those inputs to be interpreted as SQL instead of ordinary user data.

entries.name: J2EE Misconfiguration: Weak Access Permissions for EJB Methods
entries.short_description: If elevated access rights are assigned to EJB methods, then an attacker can take advantage of the permissions to exploit the product.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')
entries.short_description: The product constructs all or part of an LDAP query using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended LDAP query when it is sent to a downstream component.

entries.name: Use of Uninitialized Resource
entries.short_description: The product uses or accesses a resource that has not been initialized.

entries.name: XML Injection (aka Blind XPath Injection)
entries.short_description: The product does not properly neutralize special elements that are used in XML, allowing attackers to modify the syntax, content, or commands of the XML before it is processed by an end system.

entries.name: Use of Expired File Descriptor
entries.short_description: The product uses or accesses a file descriptor after it has been closed.

entries.name: Improper Update of Reference Count
entries.short_description: The product uses a reference count to manage a resource, but it does not update or incorrectly updates the reference count.

entries.name: Improper Control of Dynamically-Identified Variables
entries.short_description: The product does not properly restrict reading from or writing to dynamically-identified variables.

entries.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
entries.short_description: The product receives input from an upstream component that specifies multiple attributes, properties, or fields that are to be initialized or updated in an object, but it does not properly control which attributes can be modified.

entries.name: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
entries.short_description: The product generates a hash for a password, but it uses a scheme that does not provide a sufficient level of computational effort that would make password cracking attacks infeasible or expensive.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an Expression Language Statement ('Expression Language Injection')
entries.short_description: The product constructs all or part of an expression language (EL) statement in a framework such as a Java Server Page (JSP) using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended EL statement before it is executed.

entries.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
entries.short_description: The web server receives a URL or similar request from an upstream component and retrieves the contents of this URL, but it does not sufficiently ensure that the request is being sent to the expected destination.

entries.name: DEPRECATED: Improper Sanitization of Custom Special Characters
entries.short_description: This entry has been deprecated. It originally came from PLOVER, which sometimes defined "other" and "miscellaneous" categories in order to satisfy exhaustiveness requirements for taxonomies. Within the context of CWE, the use of a more abstract entry is preferred in mapping situations.

entries.name: Improper Restriction of Power Consumption
entries.short_description: The product operates in an environment in which power is a limited resource that cannot be automatically replenished, but the product does not properly restrict the amount of power that its operation consumes.

entries.name: Storage of Sensitive Data in a Mechanism without Access Control
entries.short_description: The product stores sensitive information in a file system or device that does not have built-in access control.

entries.name: Improper Enforcement of Message Integrity During Transmission in a Communication Channel
entries.short_description: The product establishes a communication channel with an endpoint and receives a message from that endpoint, but it does not sufficiently ensure that the message was not modified during transmission.

entries.name: Improper Verification of Intent by Broadcast Receiver
entries.short_description: The Android application uses a Broadcast Receiver that receives an Intent but does not properly verify that the Intent came from an authorized source.

entries.name: Improper Export of Android Application Components
entries.short_description: The Android application exports a component for use by other applications, but does not properly restrict which applications can launch the component or access the data it contains.

entries.name: Use of Implicit Intent for Sensitive Communication
entries.short_description: The Android application uses an implicit intent for transmitting sensitive data to other applications.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
entries.short_description: The product uses CRLF (carriage return line feeds) as a special element, e.g. to separate lines or records, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes CRLF sequences from inputs.

entries.name: Improper Authorization in Handler for Custom URL Scheme
entries.short_description: The product uses a handler for a custom URL scheme, but it does not properly restrict which actors can invoke the handler using the scheme.

entries.name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
entries.short_description: The product constructs all or part of a code segment using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the syntax or behavior of the intended code segment.

entries.name: Improper Verification of Source of a Communication Channel
entries.short_description: The product establishes a communication channel to handle an incoming request that has been initiated by an actor, but it does not properly verify that the request is coming from the expected origin.

entries.name: Incorrectly Specified Destination in a Communication Channel
entries.short_description: The product creates a communication channel to initiate an outgoing request to an actor, but it does not correctly specify the intended destination for that actor.

entries.name: Permissive Cross-domain Security Policy with Untrusted Domains
entries.short_description: The product uses a web-client protection mechanism such as a Content Security Policy (CSP) or cross-domain policy file, but the policy includes untrusted domains with which the web client is allowed to communicate.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
entries.short_description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes code syntax before using the input in a dynamic evaluation call (e.g. "eval").

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Statically Saved Code ('Static Code Injection')
entries.short_description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes code syntax before inserting the input into an executable resource, such as a library, configuration file, or template.

entries.name: Improper Neutralization of Server-Side Includes (SSI) Within a Web Page
entries.short_description: The product generates a web page, but does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input that could be interpreted as a server-side include (SSI) directive.

entries.name: Improper Control of Filename for Include/Require Statement in PHP Program ('PHP Remote File Inclusion')
entries.short_description: The PHP application receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before its usage in "require," "include," or similar functions.
